title: feat(runtime): /ready reports cluster driver health when multi-replica is declared
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9A6psgEaEgrJbD91eQmwK9B)_

Fixes #31601

`/ready` reports the cluster driver's health on a deployment that declares multi-replica and runs the redis cluster driver: Redis unreachable answers **200 with `status: 'degraded'`** and a `cluster` entry naming the driver unreachable (PM decision D4: never 503). Child of cloud epic #3814; Claim 6727414288 (`domain:server#4`, card-thread session_01ADHkmQwuHPnJPK768Mta39).

Clause-②: yes (widening) — measured on base `1a20cbc8` (the merge base; its `http-dispatcher.ts` restored under this PR's pins) and head `ce30cfbf`: on a declared multi-node redis deployment with Redis down, base answers `200 {"status":"ready","state":"running"}` (`expected { status: 'ready', state: 'running' } to deeply equal { status: 'degraded', …(2) }`, the `200` assertion above it passing), head answers `200 {"status":"degraded","state":"running","cluster":{"driver":"redis","reachable":false,"reason":"ping-failed"}}` (also with a live redis-server stopped, below). Every request keeps the status code base answered; the `200` body gains a `cluster` key and the `degraded` value of `status` only behind the declaration plus the redis driver. Nothing base accepted is refused.
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：声明多副本(`OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` 或 `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS>1`)且集群驱动是 redis 时，`/ready` 的 200 响应多一个 `cluster` 条目；Redis 不可达时 `status` 变为 `degraded`,仍是 200。
- 为什么改：之前 Redis 停了，各副本的 `/ready` 一直是普通的 200,运维看不到集群已失去协调(锁、计数器、跨副本事件全失效)。不用 503 是 D4 的决定：所有副本同时失去 Redis,503 会把整个集群摘出负载均衡。
- 风险与回滚：单节点、memory 驱动、没有 cluster 服务时 body 与状态码逐字节不变，也不会去 ping Redis;启动中/停机(SIGTERM)的 503 和主数据源 503 在探测前返回，不变。探测是一次 500ms 上限的 PING,缓存 1 秒。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`(`clusterReadiness()` 与两个 200 分支)、`packages/services/service-cluster/src/driver-health.ts`、`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ready.test.ts` 新增的 describe。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/http-dispatcher.ready.test.ts` —— 预期 41 passed。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **`packages/services/service-cluster/src/driver-health.ts`** (new) — `probeClusterDriverHealth(cluster, driver, { timeoutMs })`: reads the connection the driver offers (`readClusterDriverConnection`, the seam the shared cache already reads), sends one `PING` bounded by `DEFAULT_CLUSTER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` (500 ms), and answers `{ driver, reachable: true }` on `PONG`, or `{ driver, reachable: false, reason }` with `reason` from a closed set: `timeout`, `ping-failed`, `unexpected-reply`, `no-probe`. Answers `undefined` when the cluster offers no connection for that driver (memory driver, no cluster). Never throws. The client's error text (it names the store's host and port) is never carried, because `/ready` answers anonymous callers. Exported from the package index with its types.
- **`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`** — `clusterReadiness()`: applies only when `declaresMultiNode(process.env)` holds (the split-brain guard's predicate) AND the host kernel's `cluster` service offers a `redis` connection; memoized on the same 1 s TTL as the data-driver probe. It is consulted on the two `200` branches only, through `withClusterReading()`, which returns the body object as given when there is no reading. The booting/stopping `503` and the primary-datasource `503` return before it.
- **`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ready.test.ts`** — new top-level describe in the existing `/ready` harness (no existing assertion edited): the card's four acceptance cases plus secondary-degraded beside Redis down, the primary `503` never probing Redis, the memo, and R3's "one half missing" cases (no declaration, `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=1`, memory driver, no cluster service, a throwing lookup).
- **`packages/services/service-cluster/src/driver-health.test.ts`** (new) — the probe's eight readings, including a late rejection after the timeout not leaking as unhandled.
- **`.changeset/31601-ready-cluster-driver-health.md`** — `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/service-cluster` `patch`, both declaration lines, who sees it.

No test was forced to change.

<details><summary>Real Redis smoke: a live redis-server and the real ioredis driver behind /ready</summary>

A one-off script (not committed): `defineCluster({ driver: 'redis', url })` from the built `@objectstack/service-cluster-redis`, the built `HttpDispatcher`, a fresh dispatcher per probe, a `redis-server` this run started and stopped.

```text
OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=3
redis UP     : 200 {"status":"ready","state":"running","cluster":{"driver":"redis","reachable":true}} (21 ms)
redis-server stopped
redis DOWN #1: 200 {"status":"degraded","state":"running","cluster":{"driver":"redis","reachable":false,"reason":"ping-failed"}} (188 ms)
redis DOWN #2: 200 {"status":"degraded","state":"running","cluster":{"driver":"redis","reachable":false,"reason":"timeout"}} (501 ms)
redis BACK   : 200 {"status":"ready","state":"running","cluster":{"driver":"redis","reachable":true}} (2 ms)

no declaration (single node), same sequence
redis UP     : 200 {"status":"ready","state":"running"} (14 ms)
redis DOWN #1: 200 {"status":"ready","state":"running"} (1 ms)
redis DOWN #2: 200 {"status":"ready","state":"running"} (1 ms)
redis BACK   : 200 {"status":"ready","state":"running"} (1 ms)
```

The first probe after the stop reads `ping-failed` (ioredis gives up after `maxRetriesPerRequest: 3`); later ones read `timeout` (the client queues while reconnecting) and are bounded at 500 ms. Recovery needs no restart.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (each through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs; restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty git diff HEAD)</summary>

The runtime test imports `./http-dispatcher.js` from source and the service-cluster test imports `./driver-health.js` from source, so no leg needed a rebuild or a dist preflight.

| Leg | Mutation | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 R3 declaration half | `if (declaresMultiNode(…))` → `if (true)` | red: 3 single-node pins (`no declaration … no ping`, `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=1`, `#13408 body, no cluster key`) |
| A2 D4 not 503 | unreachable store answers `503 Cluster unavailable` | red: `Redis down: 200 — not 503 …` |
| A3 SIGTERM / booting 503 | probe the cluster before the kernel-state 503 and fold it into `details` | red: all four `kernel idle/initializing/stopping/stopped` pins |
| A4 primary 503 | probe the cluster on the primary-datasource drain branch | red: `… byte-identical 503, and never probes Redis` (`expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`). The first attempt was refused by the tool (the replacement contained the anchor, anchor count 1 → 1) and ran no test; re-run with a different anchor. |
| A5 no-probe never healthy | `no-probe` → `reachable: true` | red: `reads an offered client with no ping() as no-probe — never as healthy` |
| A6 address never leaks | nested: keep the client error, serve its message as `reason` | red: both `ping-failed` pins (the closed-reason `toEqual` reds before the `not.toContain('10.0.0.7')` line is reached) |

After the run: `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` clean apart from the then-uncommitted changeset.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **F3a's seam.** #31596 (Redis disconnect without crashing, reconnect and resync; seat 1) was not merged and had no PR at the time of this card, so the probe pings the driver's offered connection itself, as the dispatch said. `probeClusterDriverHealth` lives in `@objectstack/service-cluster` beside `readClusterDriverConnection` so F3a can feed or replace it in one place; `/ready` only reads the `ClusterDriverHealth` shape.
- **Observed, not changed (F3a's ground):** with Redis stopped, ioredis logs `[ioredis] Unhandled error event: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED …` on every reconnect attempt because the driver's client has no `error` listener. That is #31596's subject; this diff adds no listener.
- **`status: 'degraded'` vs the #13408 secondary branch.** A degraded SECONDARY datasource still answers `status: 'ready'` with a `degraded` object (unchanged, single node included). The cluster reading uses `status: 'degraded'` as the card and D4 specify. When both hold on a declared deployment, `status` is `degraded` and both entries are present. Unifying the two was out of scope (it would change a single-node body).
- **Docs not in the file surface.** `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx` (the `GET /ready` block) and `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` (the probe table) do not yet mention the `cluster` entry; the claim's file surface excludes `content/docs/**`, so this is left to the seat.
- **No published schema.** `/ready`'s body has no schema in `packages/spec` (searched before the first edit), so nothing in the spec moves.
- The README "multi-node unsupported" line and the split-brain guard are untouched (R3).
